Django adds three things around it (`django/http/request.py:QueryDict.__init__`).
A query string is ordinarily URL-encoded, and so ASCII, but some user agents misbehave and send bytes outside it (`django/http/request.py:QueryDict.__init__`).

`QueryDict.urlencode` goes the other way and writes the dictionary as a query string, every value of every key, key by key: among its callers in Django, `reverse` uses it for a query given as a `QueryDict`, and the `querystring` template tag for the parameters it has merged (`django/http/request.py:QueryDict.urlencode`, `django/urls/base.py:reverse`, `django/template/defaulttags.py:querystring`).
